title: California's 42nd Congressional District election, 2026
description: California's 42nd congressional district, covering parts of Los Angeles County (Long Beach) and Orange County (Huntington Beach and portions of Newport Beach), holds a general election on November 3, 2026. Incumbent Democrat Robert Garcia, a former Long Beach mayor and current ranking member of the House Oversight Committee, is seeking a third term after advancing from the June 2 top-two primary with 56.5% of the vote. He faces Republican Brian Burley, a Huntington Beach City School District trustee who advanced with 20.6%. The district has a Cook Partisan Voting Index of D+18 and was rated "Solid Democratic" by the Cook Political Report, though its boundaries shifted under mid-decade redistricting, adding more conservative Orange County coastal communities.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this specific general election race. Cook Political Report rates the race as "Solid D" and the district has a D+18 Cook PVI.

candidates.name: Robert Garcia
candidates.summary: Robert Garcia is the incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 42nd congressional district, first elected in 2022. He previously served two terms as mayor of Long Beach (2014-2022), was vice mayor (2012-2014), and served on the Long Beach City Council (2009-2014). In Congress, he serves as the ranking member of the House Oversight Committee. Born in Lima, Peru, Garcia immigrated to the United States at age five and became a citizen during college. He holds degrees from California State University, Long Beach (BA in Communication Studies, EdD in Educational Policy) and the University of Southern California (MA) and has taught at both institutions and Long Beach City College.

candidates.name: Brian Burley
candidates.summary: Brian Burley is a Republican candidate for U.S. House in California's 42nd congressional district, having advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 20.6% of the vote. He serves as a trustee on the Huntington Beach City School District Board and works as an educational systems administrator at the University of Southern California. Burley earned his undergraduate degree in Political Economy from USC, along with three master's degrees in Public Policy, Digital Media Management, and Emergency Management. His campaign focuses on affordability, public safety, border security, and election integrity.
